title: Load and Capacity Rules
before:
1. Apply all trailer, van and shift limits under PR-06 Outbound dispatch before confirming any loading plan.
2. Treat 800 kg as the maximum gross weight for a pallet, including its load, for every capacity calculation.
3. Plan contracted curtain-side trailers on a payload of 24000 kg.
4. Plan the same trailers on 33 floor pallet positions.

Weight therefore governs full-weight loads before floor space is exhausted. Divide the payload by the maximum pallet weight and cap the result by the available floor positions for each vehicle type.

5. Load a trailer with at most 30 full-weight pallets.
6. Reject any plan that places 31 full-weight pallets on one trailer, even where empty floor positions remain visible.
7. Distribute lighter pallets by both weight and footprint. Count the total kilograms against 24000 kg first, then count occupied positions against 33 pallets before releasing the load.
8. Plan the delivery van on a payload of 1200 kg.
9. Plan the same van on 6 pallet positions.
10. Load the van with at most 1 full-weight pallets.
11. Transfer any order exceeding the van weight limit to a trailer. Never split a 800 kg pallet to meet the van payload.
12. Combine up to 6 lighter pallets in the van only where their combined gross weight remains within 1200 kg and each pallet sits on its own floor position.

Shift throughput follows directly from door availability and turnaround. Use the fixed door count and the fixed loads per door to cap bookings for each shift.

13. Operate with 4 outbound dock doors.
14. Handle 3 trailer loads per shift through each outbound door.
15. Cap outbound throughput at 360 full-weight pallets per shift.
16. Derive the shift cap as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer. Stop accepting additional full-weight pallets for the shift once the calculation reaches 360 full-weight pallets per shift.
17. Sequence trailer arrivals to protect the 3 loads per door rhythm. Hold late vehicles off the leveller rather than double-stacking pallets at the dock edge.
18. Record planned pallet count and planned gross weight on every load sheet. Compare both figures against 30 full-weight pallets for trailers and 1 full-weight pallets for the van before authorising loading.
19. Escalate any request to exceed trailer, van or shift limits through the defined release control. Move no extra pallet until a revised PR-06 Outbound dispatch plan confirms weight, positions and door capacity remain compliant.

title: Dispatchers
before:
1. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads across both daily shifts.
2. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday; dispatch cover continues through handover without gaps.
3. The building has 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller.
4. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving in Zone A, the receiving zone for unloading and goods inspection.
5. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
6. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for loading.
7. Allocation of all dock doors and carrier time slots rests with the dispatcher, who balances inbound arrivals under PR-01 Inbound receiving against outbound departures under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
8. At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading; dispatchers enforce that sequence in the booking and arrival instructions.
9. Packing output from PR-05 Packing and labelling is accepted only as staged, wrapped pallets for Zone D.
10. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers; no unwrapped pallet is released for loading.
11. Every pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg; dispatch plans all loads against that ceiling.
12. Contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg with 33 floor pallet positions.
13. A trailer therefore takes at most 30 full-weight pallets, limited by payload before floor positions are reached.
14. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg with 6 pallet positions.
15. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
16. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
17. Outbound capacity is at most 360 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated from doors, loads per shift and pallets per trailer.
18. Release decisions verify wrapping, count, door, vehicle and documentation before the trailer or van is authorised to depart.
19. Coordination with the shift supervisor, who runs one shift including floor staff and incident response, keeps loading labour, MHE and staging aligned to the door plan.
20. Escalation for operations, safety and final sign-offs goes to the warehouse manager, who is accountable for the whole site.

title: Dispatch Hours, Capacity and Release
before:
1. Dispatch operates from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. All packed pallets released from PR-05 Packing and labelling are staged in Zone D only against a confirmed load and door assignment.
2. Standard dispatch hours are Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday. No loading, staging or carrier release is committed outside these hours unless overtime has been approved in advance.
3. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime. Requests for extended dispatch, additional shifts or weekend working are submitted to the warehouse manager with reason, hours, headcount and cost centre before the overtime starts.
4. The building has 8 dock doors, each fitted with a dock leveller. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch exclusively, giving 4 outbound dock doors available for loading in every staffed shift.
5. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers, and no trailer or van is staged or loaded without that assignment.
6. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. On that basis we commit a standard outbound capacity of at most 360 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer.
7. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 800 kg, so a trailer takes at most 30 full-weight pallets, limited by payload and capped by floor positions.
8. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg and has 6 pallet positions. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; any consignment exceeding that weight or volume is scheduled by trailer.
9. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in the packing-to-dispatch flow. Every outbound pallet presented in Zone D will have been wrapped, labelled, counted and system-released before loading.
10. Release of an outbound load is confirmed only after wrapping, count, door, vehicle and documentation verification. The dispatcher releases the load in the system once those checks match, and authorises departure of the trailer or van.
